hook.convey: one whole (a roti, a drawn circle) cut and shared → fair only if the pieces are the same size; equal pieces of one whole get the names half, third, quarter; the number of pieces alone does not decide the name

use.hi: Socho, Maa ne kitchen mein ek garam roti banayi, aur tum do bhai-behen ho. Roti ke 2 tukde honge. Par dono ka hissa sach mein barabar kab hota hai? Aaj wahi pakadna hai.
use.en: Picture it: Mum just made a hot roti in the kitchen, and there are two of you. The roti becomes 2 pieces. But when are both shares really equal? That's what we catch today.

use.hi: Drawing book kholo aur ek gol circle banao. Usko barabar hisson mein baantenge, phir ek hissa colour karenge. Us rangin hisse ka bhi ek naam hota hai, woh dhoondhenge.
use.en: Open your drawing book and draw a round circle. We'll split it into equal parts and colour one part. That coloured part has a name too, and we'll find it.

explain.convey: roti cut into 2 same-size pieces → each piece = half = 1/2; bottom 2 = equal pieces in the whole, top 1 = pieces taken

point.hi: Yeh roti dekho. 2 barabar tukde, aur ek tukde mein rang hai. Woh tukda roti ka aadha hai, likhte hain 1/2. Neeche ka 2, roti ke kul barabar tukde. Upar ka 1, jitne tukde humne liye.
point.en: Look at this roti. 2 equal pieces, and one piece is coloured. That piece is half the roti, and we write it 1/2. The 2 at the bottom: all the roti's equal pieces. The 1 on top: the pieces we took.

prompt.hi: Ek tukda rangin hai, ek bina rang ka. Toh kya rangin hissa 1/1 hua, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: One piece is coloured, one is not. So is the coloured part 1/1, yes or no?

why.hi: rangin tukda roti ke 2 barabar tukdon mein se 1 hai, toh woh 1/2 hai, 1/1 nahi
why.en: the coloured piece is 1 of the roti's 2 equal pieces, so it is 1/2, not 1/1

simpler.hi: Neeche wala number saare tukde ginta hai, rangin bhi aur saade bhi, yahan kul 2. Upar sirf rangin wale.
simpler.en: The bottom number counts every piece, coloured and plain, here 2 in all. The top counts only the coloured ones.

explain.convey: both cakes have 3 pieces, but only same-size pieces get the name third; Cake A uneven → no thirds; Cake B equal → each piece 1/3

point.hi: Do cake hain, dono ke 3-3 tukde. Cake A mein ek tukda bada hai aur do chhote, toh uska koi tukda 1/3 nahi. Cake B ke teeno tukde barabar hain. Wahan har tukda ek-tihaai hai, 1/3.
point.en: Two cakes, 3 pieces each. Cake A has one big piece and two small, so none of its pieces is 1/3. Cake B's three pieces are equal. There each piece is one-third, 1/3.

prompt.hi: Pizza ki baat karein. Uske 3 tukde hue, ek bada aur do chhote. Ek chhota tukda pizza ka ek-tihaai hai, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: Now a pizza. It's cut into 3 pieces, one big and two small. Is a small piece one-third of the pizza, yes or no?

accept: no, the pieces are not equal

why.hi: pizza ke tukde chhote-bade hain, aur ek-tihaai tabhi banta hai jab 3 tukde barabar hon
why.en: the pizza's pieces are big and small, and a third needs 3 equal pieces

simpler.hi: Ek chhota tukda bade tukde ke paas rakho, dono ek size ke nahi. Aise tukdon ko ek-tihaai nahi kehte.
simpler.en: Put a small piece beside the big one, and they are not the same size. Pieces like that are not called thirds.

explain.convey: drawn circle in 3 equal parts → one part = one-third = 1/3; bottom 3 = all the equal parts of the whole

point.hi: Is circle ke 3 barabar hisse hain, ek mein rang. Yeh rangin hissa ek-tihaai hai, 1/3. Neeche 3 kyun? Kyunki poore circle ke 3 barabar hisse hain.
point.en: This circle has 3 equal parts, one coloured. That coloured part is one-third, 1/3. Why 3 at the bottom? Because the whole circle has 3 equal parts.

prompt.hi: Ek aur hissa rang do. Ab circle ka kitna hissa rangin hai, fraction mein batao.
prompt.en: Colour one more part. Now what fraction of the circle is coloured?

why.hi: circle ke 3 barabar hisse hain aur ab 2 mein rang hai, yaani 2/3
why.en: the circle has 3 equal parts and 2 are coloured now, so 2/3

simpler.hi: Circle wahi hai, toh neeche 3 hi rahega. Bas upar ki ginti badlegi: jitne hisson mein rang, utna upar.
simpler.en: It is the same circle, so 3 stays at the bottom. Only the top changes: as many parts as are coloured.

explain.convey: circle in 4 equal parts, 1 shaded → one quarter = 1/4; bottom = all 4 parts of the whole, never the 3 unshaded parts left → not 1/3

point.hi: Is baar circle ke 4 barabar hisse hain. Ek mein rang, teen khaali. Rangin hissa ek-chauthaai hai, 1/4. Dhyaan do, neeche 4 aata hai, saare hisse. Bache hue 3 nahi.
point.en: This time the circle has 4 equal parts. One coloured, three empty. The coloured part is one-quarter, 1/4. Notice: 4 goes at the bottom, all the parts. Not the 3 left over.

prompt.hi: Ek pizza ke 4 barabar slice the. 1 slice kha liya, 3 bache. {friend} ka kehna hai ki 1/3 khaya gaya, kyunki 3 bache. Kya yeh sahi hai?
prompt.en: A pizza had 4 equal slices. 1 got eaten, 3 are left. {friend} says 1/3 was eaten, because 3 are left. Is that right?

why.hi: pizza ke 4 barabar slice the aur 1 khaya, toh 1/4 khaya; bache hue 3 neeche nahi jaate
why.en: the pizza had 4 equal slices and 1 was eaten, so 1/4 was eaten; the 3 left never go at the bottom

simpler.hi: Pehle poora pizza socho, khaane se pehle. Tab jitne slice the, yahan 4, wahi neeche jaate hain.
simpler.en: First picture the whole pizza, before anyone ate. However many slices it had, here 4, that goes at the bottom.

problem.hi: Ek lambi barfi ke 3 barabar tukde kiye, aur 2 tukde kha liye. Barfi ka kitna hissa khaya gaya?
problem.en: A long barfi is cut into 3 equal pieces, and 2 pieces get eaten. What fraction of the barfi was eaten?

givens.hi: Hamare paas do cheezein hain: poori barfi ke tukde, aur khaye hue tukde.
givens.en: We know two things: the pieces of the whole barfi, and the pieces eaten.

find.en: the eaten part, as a fraction

why.hi: woh poori barfi ke saare barabar tukde ginta hai
why.en: it counts all the equal pieces of the whole barfi

simpler.hi: Barfi kaatne ke baad, khaane se pehle, kitne tukde the, woh gino. Wahi ginti neeche jaati hai, yahan 3.
simpler.en: Count the pieces right after cutting, before anyone eats. That count goes at the bottom, here 3.

why.hi: woh sirf khaye hue tukde ginta hai
why.en: it counts only the pieces that were eaten

simpler.hi: Ab sirf khaye hue tukde gino, bache hue chhod do. Woh 2 hain, toh upar 2.
simpler.en: Now count only the eaten pieces and skip the rest. That's 2, so 2 on top.

prompt.hi: Dono numbers ko ek saath likho, beech mein line. Barfi ka kitna hissa khaya gaya?
prompt.en: Write the two numbers together with a line between them. What fraction of the barfi was eaten?

simpler.hi: Upar ka number tumne abhi nikala, 2. Neeche ka bhi, 3. Bas dono ko ek fraction mein likh do.
simpler.en: You already found the top, 2, and the bottom, 3. Just put them into one fraction.

why.hi: 3 barabar tukdon mein se 2 khaye gaye; bacha hua 1 tukda neeche nahi jaata
why.en: 2 of the 3 equal pieces were eaten; the 1 piece left over does not go at the bottom

prompt.hi: Laddoo toota aur 3 tukde ho gaye, ek bada aur do chhote. Kya har tukda laddoo ka ek-tihaai hai?
prompt.en: A laddoo broke into 3 pieces, one big and two small. Is each piece one-third of the laddoo?

accept: no, the pieces are not equal

why.hi: laddoo ke 3 tukde ek size ke nahi, ek bada hai aur do chhote
why.en: the laddoo's 3 pieces are not the same size: one big, two small

simpler.hi: Bade tukde ko dekho, phir chhote ko. Ek-tihaai wale tukde hamesha ek hi size ke hote hain.
simpler.en: Look at the big piece, then a small one. Thirds are always the same size.

prompt.hi: Tumhari chocolate ke 3 barabar tukde hue, aur tumne 1 kha liya. Chocolate ka kitna hissa khaya, fraction mein batao.
prompt.en: Your chocolate splits into 3 equal pieces, and you eat 1. What fraction of the chocolate did you eat?

why.hi: chocolate ke 3 barabar tukdon mein se 1 khaya, yaani 1/3
why.en: you ate 1 of the chocolate's 3 equal pieces, so 1/3

simpler.hi: Poori chocolate ke tukde neeche, jo khaya woh upar. Bas itna gino.
simpler.en: All the chocolate's pieces at the bottom, what you ate on top. Just count those.

prompt.hi: Cake ke 4 tukde hue, 1 bada aur 3 chhote. {friend} ne ek chhota tukda liya. Kya woh cake ka ek-chauthaai hai?
prompt.en: A cake is cut into 4 pieces, 1 big and 3 small. {friend} takes a small one. Is it one quarter of the cake?

accept: no, the pieces are not equal

why.hi: ek-chauthaai ke liye 4 barabar tukde chahiye, aur yahan ek tukda baaki sab se bada hai
why.en: a quarter needs 4 equal pieces, and here one piece is bigger than the rest

simpler.hi: Agar 4 tukde barabar hote, toh sab ek jaise dikhte. Yahan ek tukda alag hai, bada.
simpler.en: If the 4 pieces were equal, they would all look alike. Here one piece stands out, bigger.

ladder.why: name one of 4 equal pieces → quarter, 1/4; warm-up naming
more than one part taken → 3 of 4 equal parts = 3/4; top number beyond 1
same count of pieces, different sizes → only equal pieces are thirds
error spot: parts left used as bottom → bottom = whole's equal parts
harder contrast with quarters on flags → equality decides, count alone does not

remediation.move: fair-sharing story: one watermelon cut as 1 big slice + 2 small → fair? no → no slice has a fraction name; then a paper strip folded into 8 same-size parts → each part is 1/8 → only same-size parts carry a fraction name

say.hi: Ek tarbooz socho: 1 bada tukda, 2 chhote tukde. Yeh baant barabar nahi, isliye kisi tukde ka fraction naam nahi banta. Ab kaagaz ki patti mod kar 8 barabar hisse banao: har hissa 1/8 hai.
say.en: Think of a watermelon: 1 big piece, 2 small pieces. That's not a fair split, so no piece gets a fraction name. Now fold a paper strip into 8 equal parts, and each part is 1/8.

simpler.hi: Tukde ek size ke hon, tabhi naam milta hai, jaise patti ka 1/8. Chhote-bade tukdon ka koi naam nahi.
simpler.en: Pieces get a name only when they are the same size, like the strip's 1/8. Big-and-small pieces get no name.

prompt.hi: Roti tootkar 2 tukde ho gayi, ek bada, ek chhota. Kya chhota tukda roti ka aadha hai?
prompt.en: A roti tears into 2 pieces, one bigger, one smaller. Is the smaller piece half the roti?

why.hi: aadhe ke liye dono tukde barabar chahiye, aur yahan ek bada hai, ek chhota
why.en: a half needs both pieces equal, and here one is bigger than the other

simpler.hi: Dono tukde ek doosre ke upar rakho. Agar ek bahar nikle, toh woh aadhe nahi hain.
simpler.en: Lay one piece on top of the other. If one sticks out, they are not halves.

remediation.move: switch from chocolate bar to a round roti cut into 4 equal sectors: whole roti first → its equal pieces give the bottom number; eaten pieces give the top; pieces left are a different question, never the bottom

say.hi: Chalo, ek gol roti lete hain, 4 barabar tukde. Poori roti ke 4 tukde neeche jaate hain. Khaya hua 1 rangin tukda upar. Bache hue tukdon ka neeche koi kaam nahi.
say.en: Let's take a round roti, 4 equal pieces. The whole roti's 4 pieces go at the bottom. The 1 coloured piece that was eaten goes on top. The leftover pieces have no job at the bottom.

simpler.hi: Khaane se pehle roti ke kitne tukde the, woh gino: woh 4 neeche. Phir sirf khaya hua gino: woh 1 upar.
simpler.en: Count the roti's pieces before eating: that 4 goes at the bottom. Then count only what was eaten: that 1 goes on top.

prompt.hi: Chocolate bar ke 4 barabar tukde the, aur 3 kha liye. Bar ka kitna hissa khaya, fraction mein?
prompt.en: A chocolate bar had 4 equal pieces, and 3 got eaten. What fraction of the bar was eaten?

why.hi: bar ke 4 barabar tukdon mein se 3 khaye gaye, yaani 3/4
why.en: 3 of the bar's 4 equal pieces were eaten, so 3/4

simpler.hi: Bar kaatne par 4 tukde bane, woh neeche. Upar ke liye sirf khaye hue tukde gino.
simpler.en: Cutting the bar made 4 pieces; that goes at the bottom. For the top, count only the eaten pieces.

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab tak ek roti ke barabar hisse kiye. Ab bahut saare laddoo lenge, aur unke barabar group banayenge. Niyam wahi hai, sab barabar.
bridgeToNext.en: So far we made equal parts of one roti. Next we take lots of laddoos and make equal groups. Same rule: everything equal.

hook.convey: 8 laddoos (or 8 biscuits), 2 sharers, fair share → each share = half of the set; a fraction can be of a whole set, the set being the one whole

use.hi: Kitchen ke dibbe mein 8 laddoo rakhe hain, aur khaane wale tum do. Kisi ko kam nahi milna chahiye. 8 laddoo ka aadha kitna hota hai, aaj yahi nikalenge.
use.en: There are 8 laddoos in the kitchen tin, and two of you to eat them. Nobody should get fewer. Today we work out what half of 8 laddoos is.

use.hi: 8 biscuit hain aur 2 bhookhe puppy. Dono ko ek jitne biscuit dene hain, warna jhagda hoga. Ek puppy ko 8 ka aadha milega.
use.en: There are 8 biscuits and 2 hungry puppies. Both must get the same number, or there'll be a fight. Each puppy gets half of the 8.

explain.convey: 8 laddoos → 2 equal groups → 1/2 of 8 = one group = 4; check: 2 groups of 4 = 8

point.hi: Yeh 8 laddoo dekho, 2 barabar group mein. Har group mein 4. Ek group hi 8 ka aadha hai, toh 8 ka 1/2 = 4. Jaanch lo: 2 × 4 = 8.
point.en: Look at these 8 laddoos in 2 equal groups. 4 in each. One group is half of 8, so 1/2 of 8 = 4. Check: 2 × 4 = 8.

prompt.hi: Ab dibbe mein 12 laddoo hain. 12 ka aadha kitna hoga?
prompt.en: Now there are 12 laddoos in the tin. What is half of 12?

why.hi: 12 laddoo 2 barabar group mein jaayein toh har group mein 6, aur 2 × 6 = 12
why.en: 12 laddoos in 2 equal groups puts 6 in each, and 2 × 6 = 12

simpler.hi: 12 laddoo do plate mein ek-ek karke rakho, ek idhar, ek udhar. Khatam hone par ek plate gin lo.
simpler.en: Put the 12 laddoos on two plates one at a time, one here, one there. When they run out, count one plate.

explain.convey: 6 bananas → 3 equal groups → 1/3 of 6 = one group = 2; bottom 3 = number of equal groups, top 1 = groups taken

point.hi: Yahan 6 kele hain, 3 barabar group mein, har group mein 2. 1/3 ka neeche wala 3 kehta hai: 3 group banao. Upar ka 1: unme se ek lo. Toh 6 ka 1/3 = 2 kele.
point.en: Here are 6 bananas in 3 equal groups, 2 in each. The 3 at the bottom of 1/3 says: make 3 groups. The 1 on top: take one of them. So 1/3 of 6 = 2 bananas.

prompt.hi: 21 kele 3 bachchon mein barabar baantne hain. 21 ka 1/3 kitna hua?
prompt.en: 21 bananas to share equally among 3 children. What is 1/3 of 21?

why.hi: 21 kele 3 barabar group mein baanto toh har group mein 7 aate hain; 3 × 7 = 21
why.en: 21 bananas in 3 equal groups gives 7 in each; 3 × 7 = 21

simpler.hi: 3 ka pahada yaad karo. 3 ko kis number se guna karein ki 21 bane, wahi ek group hai.
simpler.en: Think of the 3 times table. Whatever times 3 makes 21, that is one group.

explain.convey: 12 marbles → 4 equal groups → 1/4 of 12 = one group = 3; method: bottom number → that many equal groups → size of one group is the answer

point.hi: 12 kanche, 4 barabar group, har group mein 3. Tarika seedha hai: neeche ka number dekho, utne barabar group banao, aur ek group gin lo. Toh 12 ka 1/4 = 3.
point.en: 12 marbles, 4 equal groups, 3 in each. The method is simple: look at the bottom number, make that many equal groups, and count one group. So 1/4 of 12 = 3.

prompt.hi: Kanche badh kar 32 ho gaye. 32 ka 1/4 kitna?
prompt.en: The marbles grow to 32. What is 1/4 of 32?

why.hi: 4 barabar group banao toh har group mein 8 kanche, aur 4 × 8 = 32
why.en: 4 equal groups of 32 marbles hold 8 each, and 4 × 8 = 32

simpler.hi: 4 group banane hain. 4 ke pahade mein dhoondo, kaunsa number 32 tak le jaata hai.
simpler.en: We need 4 groups. Look in the 4 times table for what gets you to 32.

problem.hi: 15 pencil ka 1/3 kitni pencil hoti hain?
problem.en: How many pencils is 1/3 of 15 pencils?

givens.hi: Kul ginti pata hai, fraction bhi pata hai; bas ek group ka size chahiye.
givens.en: We know the total and the fraction; we just need the size of one group.

find.en: how many pencils are in the 1/3 share

do.en: First think what 1/3 is telling us

steps.result: 3 barabar group, unme se 1 group lena

why.hi: neeche ka 3 group ki ginti hai, aur upar ka 1 batata hai kitne group lene hain
why.en: the bottom 3 is the number of groups, and the top 1 says how many to take

simpler.hi: Socho 3 dost hain aur pencil sabko barabar milni hain. Ek dost ka hissa hi 1/3 hai.
simpler.en: Picture 3 friends who must get equal pencils. One friend's share is the 1/3.

prompt.hi: Chalo, 15 pencil ko 3 barabar group mein baanto. 3 ka pahada kaam aayega. Ek group mein kitni pencil?
prompt.en: Go on, share the 15 pencils into 3 equal groups. The 3 times table helps. How many pencils in one group?

simpler.hi: Pencil ek-ek karke 3 dheriyon mein rakho, baari-baari. Saari khatam, toh ek dheri gin lo.
simpler.en: Put the pencils one at a time into 3 piles, taking turns. When they are gone, count one pile.

why.hi: 3 group mein 5-5 pencil rakho toh poori 15 ho jaati hain, 3 × 5 = 15
why.en: 5 pencils in each of 3 groups makes all 15, 3 × 5 = 15

prompt.hi: 18 laddoo 3 plate mein barabar rakhe gaye. Ravi ne 1 plate utha li. Saare laddoo ka kitna hissa Ravi ke paas gaya, fraction mein?
prompt.en: 18 laddoos are set out equally on 3 plates. Ravi picks up 1 plate. What fraction of all the laddoos does Ravi have?

why.hi: 18 laddoo 3 barabar plate mein the, har plate mein 6; Ravi ne 1 plate li, yaani 1/3
why.en: the 18 laddoos were on 3 equal plates, 6 on each; Ravi took 1 plate, so 1/3

simpler.hi: Laddoo mat gino, plate gino. Kul plate neeche, Ravi ki plate upar.
simpler.en: Don't count laddoos, count plates. All the plates at the bottom, Ravi's plate on top.

prompt.hi: 16 kanche 4 group mein bate: 7, 3, 3 aur 3. Kya 7 wala group saare kanchon ka ek-chauthaai hai?
prompt.en: 16 marbles went into 4 groups: 7, 3, 3 and 3. Is the group of 7 one-quarter of all the marbles?

accept: no, the groups are not equal

why.hi: group 7, 3, 3, 3 ek jaise nahi hain; 16 ka ek-chauthaai 4 hota, har group mein 4
why.en: groups 7, 3, 3, 3 are not the same; a quarter of 16 would be 4 in every group

simpler.hi: 7 wale group ko 3 wale ke paas rakho, ek jaise nahi lagte. Ek-chauthaai mein charon group ek jaise hote.
simpler.en: Put the 7 group next to a 3 group, and they don't match. In quarters, all four groups match.

ladder.why: thirds of a set as sharing among 3 friends → 3 equal groups
one-third in a word problem without the sharing story spelled out
quarters of a bigger set → 4 equal groups
name the fraction of the set and find the amount, both
two fractions of the same set in one problem → half and quarter

remediation.move: map the plates onto a bar: 3 plates ↔ bar of 3 equal parts; whole bar = all the laddoos = bottom; shaded part = Ravi's plate = top; plates left are not the bottom

say.hi: Plates ko ek patti bana dete hain. Poori patti matlab saare laddoo, aur iske 3 barabar hisse neeche ka 3. Ravi ki 1 rangin plate upar ka 1.
say.en: Let's turn the plates into a strip. The whole strip is all the laddoos, and its 3 equal parts are the bottom 3. Ravi's 1 coloured plate is the top 1.

simpler.hi: Har plate patti ka ek dabba hai. Saare dabbe neeche, Ravi ka dabba upar.
simpler.en: Each plate is one box of the strip. All the boxes at the bottom, Ravi's box on top.

prompt.hi: 24 kele 6 thailon mein barabar bhare. 1 thaila kisi ko de diya. Saare kelon ka kitna hissa diya?
prompt.en: 24 bananas are packed equally into 6 bags. 1 bag is given away. What fraction of all the bananas was given?

why.hi: 24 kele 6 barabar thailon mein the, har thaile mein 4; unme se 1 diya, yaani 1/6
why.en: the 24 bananas were in 6 equal bags, 4 in each; 1 bag went, so 1/6

simpler.hi: Har thaila ek barabar hissa hai. Saare thaile neeche jaate hain, jo diya woh upar.
simpler.en: Each bag is one equal share. All the bags go at the bottom; the one given goes on top.

remediation.move: fair-share test on the same 16 marbles: uneven groups 7 + 3 + 3 + 3 beside equal groups 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 → only equal groups make a fraction's share

say.hi: Wahi 16 kanche lo. Yeh alag group 7, 3, 3, 3 barabar nahi. Barabar baanto toh 4, 4, 4, 4 bante hain. Fraction ka hissa sirf aise barabar group se banta hai.
say.en: Take the same 16 marbles. These groups of 7, 3, 3, 3 aren't equal. Shared fairly, they make 4, 4, 4, 4. A fraction's share comes only from equal groups like that.

simpler.hi: Ek-ek kancha uthao aur 4 group mein baari-baari rakho. Har group mein 4 aayenge, yahi barabar hai.
simpler.en: Pick up one marble at a time and drop them into 4 groups in turn. Each group gets 4, and that is equal.

prompt.hi: 12 pencil ke 3 group bane: 6, 3 aur 3. Kya 6 wala group saari pencilon ka ek-tihaai hai?
prompt.en: 12 pencils made 3 groups: 6, 3 and 3. Is the group of 6 one-third of all the pencils?

why.hi: group 6, 3, 3 ek jaise nahi; 12 ka ek-tihaai 4 hota, teeno group mein 4-4
why.en: groups 6, 3, 3 don't match; a third of 12 would be 4, with 4 in each group

simpler.hi: 6 wale group ke paas 3 wala rakho, ek doosre ka double hai. Ek-tihaai mein teeno group ek size ke hote.
simpler.en: Put the 6 group beside a 3 group, and one is double the other. In thirds, all three groups are the same size.

bridgeToNext.hi: Wahi 8 laddoo phir se. 8 ka 1/2 = 4, par 8 ka 1/4 = 2. Group zyada, toh har hissa chhota. Agli baar ek hi cheez ke 1/2, 1/3 aur 1/4 ko aamne-saamne rakhenge.
bridgeToNext.en: The same 8 laddoos again. 1/2 of 8 = 4, but 1/4 of 8 = 2. More groups, smaller share. Next we put 1/2, 1/3 and 1/4 of one thing side by side.

hook.convey: one cake (or one drawn strip) shared into 2 vs the same-size one into 4 → which single piece is bigger; more equal parts of the same whole → smaller piece

use.hi: Ek birthday cake 2 dost baant rahe hain, aur bilkul waisa hi doosra cake 4 dost. Kis taraf har dost ko bada tukda milega? Aaj yahi pata karte hain.
use.en: Two friends share a birthday cake, and four friends share another one exactly like it. On which side does each friend get the bigger piece? Let's find out today.

use.hi: Do patti draw karo, dono ek jitni lambi. Ek ko 2 barabar hisson mein baanto, doosri ko 4 mein. Dono mein ek-ek hissa colour karo. Kaunsa rangin hissa bada hai, aaj dekhenge.
use.en: Draw two strips of the same length. Split one into 2 equal parts and the other into 4. Colour one part in each. We'll see which coloured part is bigger.

explain.convey: bar cut into 2 equal parts → one part = 1/2; shaded part reaches the middle of the bar; predict: same bar in 4 parts → is one part bigger than the half? no

point.hi: Yeh patti 2 barabar hisson mein bati hai. Rangin hissa iska aadha hai, 1/2. Dekho, rang theek beech tak jaata hai.
point.en: This bar is split into 2 equal parts. The coloured part is half of it, 1/2. See, the colour goes exactly to the middle.

prompt.hi: Isi patti ko ab 4 barabar hisson mein kaato. Kya tab ek hissa is aadhe se bada hoga?
prompt.en: Now cut this same bar into 4 equal parts. Will one part then be bigger than this half?

why.hi: 4 hisson mein har hissa 1/4 hota hai, jo 1/2 ka bhi aadha hai
why.en: in 4 parts each part is 1/4, which is half of the 1/2

simpler.hi: Aadhe wale hisse ko beech se ek baar aur kaato. Woh aur chhota ho jaata hai, bada nahi.
simpler.en: Cut the half once more down the middle. It gets smaller, not bigger.

explain.convey: same bar cut into 4 equal parts → one part = 1/4; shaded part much shorter than the half on the last board

point.hi: Wahi patti, ab 4 barabar hisson mein. Rangin hissa ek-chauthaai hai, 1/4. Pichhle aadhe ke saath rakho, yeh kaafi chhota hai.
point.en: The same bar, now in 4 equal parts. The coloured part is one-quarter, 1/4. Put it next to the half from before: it is much smaller.

prompt.hi: Do ek jaise pizza. Ek ke 4 barabar slice, doosre ke 2. Bada slice kaunsa fraction hai?
prompt.en: Two identical pizzas. One cut into 4 equal slices, the other into 2. What fraction is the bigger slice?

why.hi: 2 slice wale pizza ka har slice 1/2 hai, jo 4 slice wale ke 1/4 se do guna hai
why.en: each slice of the 2-slice pizza is 1/2, twice the 1/4 slice of the 4-slice pizza

simpler.hi: Pizza jitne kam logon mein bante, utna bada slice milta hai. 2 log ya 4 log, socho kisko zyada milega.
simpler.en: The fewer people share a pizza, the bigger the slice. 2 people or 4 people: think who gets more.

explain.convey: bigger bottom number → same whole cut into more parts → each part smaller → 1/2 > 1/4; 4 > 2 as whole numbers does not make 1/4 bigger; only true for the same whole

point.hi: Dono ko saath rakho. Bayein, patti ke 2 barabar hisse: ek hissa 1/2, bada tukda. Dayein, wahi patti ke 4 barabar hisse: ek hissa 1/4, chhota tukda. Seedhi baat: zyada hisse, chhota tukda.
point.en: Put them side by side. Left: the bar in 2 equal parts, one part is 1/2, a big piece. Right: the same bar in 4 equal parts, one part is 1/4, a small piece. Simply put: more parts, smaller piece.

prompt.hi: 4 toh 2 se bada number hai. Toh kya ek hi roti ka 1/4, uske 1/2 se bada hua?
prompt.en: 4 is a bigger number than 2. So is 1/4 of a roti bigger than 1/2 of the same roti?

why.hi: roti ke 4 hisse karo toh har hissa 2 hisson wale se chhota, isliye 1/4 chhota hai
why.en: cut a roti into 4 and each part is smaller than when it is cut into 2, so 1/4 is smaller

simpler.hi: Number 4 bada hai, par woh roti ke tukdon ki ginti hai. Jitne zyada tukde, har tukda utna patla.
simpler.en: 4 is the bigger number, but it counts the roti's pieces. The more pieces, the thinner each one.

problem.hi: Ek hi chocolate bar ka 1/3 bada hota hai ya 1/4?
problem.en: Of the same chocolate bar, which is bigger: 1/3 or 1/4?

givens.hi: Dono hisse ek hi bar ke hain, bar ka size nahi badalta.
givens.en: Both shares come from one bar; the bar's size does not change.

steps.result: bar ke 3 barabar hisse, unme se 1 hissa

why.hi: bar ke kitne barabar hisse hue, yeh neeche ka 3 batata hai
why.en: the bottom 3 says how many equal parts the bar is in

simpler.hi: Bar ko 3 dost baant rahe hain. Ek dost ka tukda, wahi 1/3 hai.
simpler.en: 3 friends share the bar. One friend's piece is the 1/3.

steps.result: wahi bar ke 4 barabar hisse, unme se 1 hissa

why.hi: wahi bar ab 4 mein bat rahi hai, toh har hissa chhota padta hai
why.en: the same bar is now shared by 4, so each share comes out smaller

simpler.hi: Ab wahi bar 4 dost baant rahe hain. Ek dost aur aa gaya, toh sabka tukda thoda chhota.
simpler.en: Now 4 friends share the same bar. One more friend joined, so everyone's piece shrinks a bit.

prompt.hi: Dono tukdon ko saath rakh kar dekho. Bada tukda kaunsa fraction hai?
prompt.en: Put the two pieces side by side. Which fraction is the bigger piece?

simpler.hi: 3 dost ya 4 dost, bar ek hi hai. Kam dost hon toh har ek ko bada tukda milta hai.
simpler.en: 3 friends or 4 friends, the same bar. Fewer friends means a bigger piece for each.

answer.en: 1/3 of the chocolate bar is bigger: 1/3 > 1/4

why.hi: 4 hisson wala tukda 3 hisson wale tukde se chhota hai, chahe 4 bada number ho
why.en: a piece from 4 parts is smaller than a piece from 3, even though 4 is the bigger number

prompt.hi: Do roti hain, ek hi size ki. Pehli ke 3 barabar tukde kiye, doosri ke 2 barabar tukde. Sabse bada tukda kaunsa fraction hai?
prompt.en: Two rotis of the same size. The first is cut into 3 equal pieces, the second into 2 equal pieces. Which fraction is the biggest piece?

why.hi: jo roti 2 mein kati, uska har tukda 1/2 hai, aur woh 1/3 se bada hai
why.en: the roti cut in 2 has pieces of 1/2, and that is bigger than 1/3

simpler.hi: Dono roti ek size ki hain. Jo roti kam tukdon mein kati, uske tukde mote hain.
simpler.en: Both rotis are the same size. The one cut into fewer pieces has fatter pieces.

prompt.hi: Ek chocolate bar 4 bachchon mein barabar bati, aur utni hi badi doosri bar 2 bachchon mein. Farhan 4 waalon mein hai. Woh kehta hai, mujhe zyada mili, kyunki 4 bada hai. Kya Farhan sahi hai?
prompt.en: One chocolate bar is shared equally by 4 children, and a bar the same size by 2. Farhan is with the 4. He says he got more, because 4 is bigger. Is Farhan right?

why.hi: 4 mein bati bar ka har hissa 1/4 hai, 2 waalon ke 1/2 ka aadha, toh Farhan ko kam mila
why.en: shared by 4, each share is 1/4, half of the 1/2 the pair get, so Farhan got less

simpler.hi: Ek hi bar ko jitne zyada bachche baantein, har bachche ka hissa utna patla. Farhan ki taraf 4 bachche hain.
simpler.en: The more children share the same bar, the thinner each share. Farhan's side has 4 children.

prompt.hi: Ek hi chocolate bar ke teen tukde: 1/2, 1/4 aur 1/3. Inhe sabse chhote se sabse bade tak lagao.
prompt.en: Three pieces of the same chocolate bar: 1/2, 1/4 and 1/3. Put them in order from smallest to biggest.

why.hi: bar jitne zyada hisson mein kate, tukda utna chhota; isliye pehle 1/4, phir 1/3, phir 1/2
why.en: the more parts a bar is cut into, the smaller the piece, so 1/4 first, then 1/3, then 1/2

simpler.hi: Sabse chhota tukda woh, jiski bar sabse zyada hisson mein kati. Wahan se shuru karo.
simpler.en: The smallest piece comes from the bar cut into the most parts. Start there.

ladder.why: quick recall: 1/2 vs 1/4 of the same pizza
predict from a sharing story → 2 sharers vs 3 sharers, halves vs thirds
explain the rule in words → bottom number = number of equal parts, more parts → smaller each
order three unit fractions of one whole, biggest first
link back to collections → 1/3 and 1/4 of 12 slices as amounts, then the difference

remediation.move: fraction bars of the same length, one in 5 equal parts, one in 10 → predict the longer single piece → lay one piece from each side by side → more cuts of the same bar → each piece shorter

say.hi: Kaagaz ki patti ke 5 barabar hisse karo, toh 1 hissa 1/5 hai, lamba tukda. Wahi patti ke 10 hisse karo, toh 1 hissa 1/10, chhota tukda. Jitne zyada hisse, utna chhota tukda.
say.en: Cut a paper bar into 5 equal parts and 1 part is 1/5, a long piece. Cut the same bar into 10 and 1 part is 1/10, a short piece. The more parts, the smaller the piece.

simpler.hi: Dono tukde saath rakho: 1/5 wala lamba hai, 1/10 wala chhota. Neeche ka number bada, toh tukda chhota.
simpler.en: Lay the two side by side: the 1/5 is long, the 1/10 is short. Bigger bottom number, smaller piece.

prompt.hi: Do ek jaise cake: ek ke 8 barabar tukde, doosre ke 6 barabar tukde. Rahul kehta hai 8 wala tukda bada hai. Sahi hai?
prompt.en: Two same cakes: one in 8 equal slices, one in 6 equal slices. Rahul says the 8-cake slice is bigger. Is he right?

why.hi: 8 tukdon wale cake ka har tukda 1/8 hai, jo 6 tukdon wale ke 1/6 se chhota hai
why.en: each slice of the 8-slice cake is 1/8, smaller than the 1/6 slice of the 6-slice cake

simpler.hi: 8 log ek cake baant rahe hain, 6 log doosra. Zyada log, chhota tukda.
simpler.en: 8 people share one cake, 6 share the other. More people, smaller piece.
